purpose: Close the pilot's two review-failed rebuilds now that the game's x87 precision control is measured and the export keeps CR, and give the Havok step planner a second mapping pass against the measured run.

functions.name: PlanHavokSteps (proposal from time-info; second pass)
functions.known: A mapping exists: re/functions/0x00889810.md (time-info slice) - start from it. It reads the function as a scheduler over globals: frame seconds + carry 0x00BA7910 -> step count 0x00BA7914 and step length 0x00BA790C, dispatched on the update type 0x00BA7918 as 0 = fixed step 0x00B2E2E8 with carry, 10 = smoothed 0x00B2E2EC, else the whole time split into equal steps; cap 3 or 2 steps. MEASURED in the game (2026-10-27, Linux, 75 Hz = 13.33 ms frames, OBNG.dll sampling 0x00BA7918 and 0x00BA7914 once a frame and reading 0x00BA790C at the summary): update type 0 the whole run; in play 1 step on 99.5 % of the frames, 2 on the rest, never 0; the step length read 0.013333 s = the frame's length, not 0.016667. The image values from data.json: 0x00B2E2E8 = 0.016666668f, 0x00B2E2E4 = 0.016f, 0x00B2E2E0 = 0.016f, 0x00B2E2EC = 0.032f, 0x00B2E2F0 = 0.05f, 0x00A95CA8 = 0.008333334f; runtime values of the writable ones unverified (OBVR: 0x00B2E2E8 is the runtime copy of fMaxTime:HAVOK). The static reading of the type-0 branch does not produce these numbers (a fixed 1/60 step with carry would give 0 steps on some frames and a step of 16.67 ms). Re-read the dispatch and the type-0 branch against asm.s with these measurements as the ground truth: which branch gives one step of the frame's own length at 13.33 ms, and under what condition that branch is reached with type 0. Also read the 2-step frames: which input makes them.
questions: Which branch of the planner runs under update type 0 at 13.33 ms frames, and why does it give one step of the frame's length?
What is the role of 0x00B2E2E8 (1/60 in the image) in that branch - a cap on the step, a divisor, or unused?
What makes a 2-step frame (0.5 % of the frames at 75 Hz)?
Would a 90 Hz frame (11.1 ms) under the same branch give one step of 11.1 ms, or does something else apply?

functions.name: LoadingMenu::Tick (confirmed in frame-clock; rebuild rejected in review)
functions.known: Mapping: re/functions/0x005AD980.md (confirmed in the pilot's second round) - start from it; the TimeInfo field names are now freezeDepth, fixedStepMs, fixedStepCarryMs, frameSeconds, clockMs, startTick (src/engine/time/TimeInfo.h), the menu's private TimeInfo at Menu+0x54. A rebuild exists: src/engine/time/LoadingMenu_TickLogic.h, LoadingMenu_Tick.h, tests/LoadingMenu_TickTest.cpp (20 flows, green) - REVISE THESE FILES IN PLACE. It was rejected by the correctness review because the countdown arithmetic matched the original only at x87 precision control 53-bit, with inputs that differ at 24-bit (timer 5.0, sinceLast -100). MEASURED 2026-10-27: the game runs the x87 at 24-bit precision control, rounding to nearest (_control87 0x000A001F, read at the first TimeInfo::Update under Proton). The rebuild must therefore reproduce the 24-bit x87 arithmetic of the instructions (every intermediate rounded to float where the x87 would at PC=24; note that loads of doubles from memory still hold their double value in the register but every arithmetic result is rounded to 24-bit mantissa), and the tests must include the review's inputs. Constants now in data.json (0x00A2FC70 etc.). The export's strings keep CR LF.
questions: Which x87 operations in the countdown round at 24-bit, and what does the rebuild have to do to match (float intermediates, or explicit rounding of double results)?
What is the double at 0x00A2FC70 (the timer's unit)?
